findings.source_quote: καὶ πανούργως ὑποσπείροντι ὑμῖν τὰς θεῷ ἐχθραινούσας ὑπονοίας
findings.english_quote: and cunningly sowing notions hostile to God
findings.issue: The recipient expressed by ὑμῖν is not explicitly represented in this clause. The preceding 'within you' describes where the evil lurks, rather than expressly identifying those into whom it sows these notions.
findings.suggested_revision: Render 'and cunningly sowing in you notions hostile to God'.

findings.source_quote: ὑπονοίᾳ γὰρ φρονήσεως τὴν ἄγνοιαν κρατύνει.
findings.english_quote: through a pretension to intelligence, it strengthens ignorance.
findings.issue: ὑπόνοια denotes a supposition, suspicion, or notion. 'Pretension' shifts this toward a claim or display of intelligence, whereas the Greek describes ignorance being strengthened through supposed understanding.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a rendering such as 'for through supposed understanding, it strengthens ignorance'. This also restores the explanatory γάρ. Any revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ οἶμαι, εἰ τοῦτο λέγων τις ἐρεῖ βασιλεῖ Τὴν ἴσην σοι ἀπονέμω τιμήν, οἵαν καὶ τοῖς νεκροῖς καὶ τῇ ἐρριμμένῃ κοπρίᾳ· οὐκ οἴομαι εἰ καλῶς ἀπαλλάξει.
findings.english_quote: I do not think that someone who says this to a king—“I assign you the same honor as I do the dead and discarded dung”—will come off well.
findings.issue: The draft compresses the two printed negative assertions, οὐκ οἶμαι and οὐκ οἴομαι, into one. It also smooths the conditional construction and syntactic restart without disclosure. The overall conclusion survives, but the selected edition's repeated assertion does not.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve both assertions and the conditional, for example: 'I do not think so—if someone who says this tells a king, “I assign you the same honor as I do the dead and discarded dung,” I do not think he will come off well.' Explain the repeated construction as a feature of the supplied wording, not an OCR error. This candidate requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: κἂν λῃστοῦ τις ἢ πατρὸς ἢ αἰσχροβίου
findings.english_quote: even if someone’s father is a robber or leads a shameful life
findings.issue: The draft makes πατρὸς the common noun qualified by 'robber' and 'shameful life', but the supplied wording places it after a printed ἢ and before another ἢ. The note calls the construction compressed without explaining how both conjunctions are represented. The draft effectively reads past the first disjunction. The print is already image-checked; this is not an unverified OCR reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain both printed disjunctions under an explicitly disclosed elliptical interpretation. One provisional candidate is 'even if someone is the child of a robber, or of a father, or of a man who lives shamefully', with a note explaining that the child relationship is inferred from the following ὁ υἱός and that the redundant 'father' remains the supplied reading. If proposing ᾖ instead of the first ἢ, identify that as a conjectural correction, not the edition's text. The replacement must receive fresh review.

findings.source_quote: οὐκ ὀφείλει ὁ υἱὸς νήψας τὸ κρεῖττον ἑλέσθαι, ἵνα μὴ ἀσεβήσῃ καὶ μὴ τὰ ἴσα τοῖς γονεῦσιν ποιῶν ἀμαρτάνῃ;
findings.english_quote: should the son not become clear-minded and choose what is better, lest he act impiously and sin by not doing the same things as his parents?
findings.issue: νήψας is a participial circumstance: the son chooses after becoming clear-minded. The draft turns it into a second action governed by 'should'. Moreover, the English negative question readily sounds like an exhortation to choose better, although the sentence is testing the consequence of the preceding ancestral-practice argument. That rhetorical difficulty is not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the participle circumstantial: 'once he has become clear-minded'. Explain the rhetorical scope of οὐκ ὀφείλει under τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ, including the alternatives 'is not obliged to choose' and 'is not to choose'. A provisional contextual formulation is 'by this reasoning ... is the son, once clear-minded, not to choose the better course, lest ...?' Do not certify this formulation without fresh review.

findings.english_quote: do you all look toward heaven
findings.issue: τὰ πάντα is neuter accusative, not the nominative πάντες that would directly mean 'you all'. It qualifies the looking or its scope rather than plainly quantifying the people looking.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep τὰ πάντα with the act or scope of looking. Candidates include 'looking wholly toward heaven' and 'looking to heaven for everything'; document the chosen attachment and preserve the viable alternative.

findings.source_quote: ὅπως τὰς αὐτῶν ὀφειλομένας εὐχὰς καὶ εὐχαριστίας καὶ νεκρῶν νεκροτέροις προσενέγκητε;
findings.english_quote: so that you offer your owed prayers and thanksgivings to things deader even than the dead?
findings.issue: αὐτῶν is third-person plural, while προσενέγκητε is second-person plural. The draft silently changes 'their' to 'your'. Identifying the addressed audience with the previously mentioned senseless people is contextually defensible, but the source's pronoun shift and the alternative antecedent relationship are not preserved or explained.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare the source-transparent candidate 'so that you offer their owed prayers and thanksgivings to things deader even than the dead'. Add a note explaining that αὐτῶν can refer to the senseless people and that these may include the audience. If retaining 'your', explicitly justify that identification and preserve the third-person alternative.

findings.source_quote: ἡ κνίσα ῥεμβομένη καὶ τὰ τυφλὰ καὶ κωφὰ πνεύματα διὰ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἄγει εἰς τὸν τῆς ὀσφρήσεως αὐτῶν τόπον.
findings.english_quote: Their drifting sacrificial smoke, through its power, brings even the blind and deaf spirits to the place where they smell it.
findings.issue: The smoke is the grammatical subject, but διὰ τῆς ἐξουσίας does not expressly identify the possessor or source of the power. 'Its power' is a defensible contextual interpretation, yet the note presents attribution to the smoke as something explicitly retained from the Greek rather than an interpretive choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Either retain 'through its power' with a note explaining the inferred attribution and preserving 'through the power/authority' without a specified possessor, or use the less committal wording in the main text. Do not introduce an independently specified divine or demonic source of that authority.

findings.english_quote: by your own hand, by a stroke
findings.issue: αὐτοχειρίᾳ can denote self-killing or killing performed with one's own hand. The draft selects the victims' self-killing through 'your', although the expressed agents of the surrounding sentence are the demons. The existing note neither explains that agency choice nor preserves the alternative. The self-killing interpretation is contextually defensible and does not itself require blocking.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note explaining that 'by your own hand' understands the demons as inducing the victims to kill themselves, supported contextually by the listed pretexts and means of death. Preserve the alternative of direct killing by the demons themselves. Any change to the main rendering must undergo fresh review.
